This misinterprets the criterion, which asks about their status when they joined.

The plan in Step 1 correctly targeted roles at the time of joining the board, but in Step 7 the agent shifted to assessing whether a member had ever held a C-suite role “before joining,” which is a different standard. This is the first explicit deviation from the correct criterion, and it propagated to all subsequent assessments, leading to the incorrect conclusion.

Yes, the mistake persisted. Subsequent steps repeated this criterion (e.g., Wanda Austin, Ronald D. Sugar, Susan L. Wagner), and the DataVerification_Expert (step 21) reinforced the same misinterpretation. No later step corrected the timing criterion, leading to the incorrect final conclusion.
